#5757. Fierce Healthcare Fundraising Tracker '26: Aevius launches with $22M for clinical insights; Abby Care secures $82M for family-led care

Fierce Healthcare Fundraising Tracker '26: Aevius launches with $22M for clinical insights; Abby Care secures $82M for family-led care" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

At Fierce Healthcare, we keep track of all the venture capital being funneled into the health tech and digital health industries.

Our fundraising tracker provides updated coverage of noteworthy digital health and health tech funding rounds, though we'll still profile exciting new companies and larger rounds that catch our eye in depth.

Do you have fundraising news to share? Email Heather Landi at [email protected].

Oct. 17—AeviusClinical intelligence AI modelsSeries: N/AAmount: $22 millionInvestors: Led by Insight Partners

Aevius is a newly launched Mass General Brigham spinout founded by veterans of AstreaZeneca-acquired Modella AI. The company builds models that intake different forms of medical data to paint a multimodal picture of a patient's current state and trajectory. That information can then be used by healthcare, payer and life sciences organizations for potential application in care delivery, operational decision-making and clinical research.

“Our mission is to make medicine computable,” Rowland Pettit, M.D., Ph.D., co-founder and CEO of Aevius, said. “As a physician-scientist, I’ve worked across many types of clinical data, and there is far more knowledge in those records than we’re able to use today. We’re bringing general medical intelligence to that data, so organizations can build on a deeper understanding for their patients.”

The company said it plans to use the $22 million launch money to support continued model and product development. It also plans to expand its engineering, clinical and commercial teams, as well as to focus on commercial deployment.

Oct. 15—Abby CareFamily caregiver trainingSeries: CAmount: $82 millionInvestors: Led by Transformation Capital, along with CVS Health Ventures, Frist Cressey Ventures and Pivotal, with participation from existing investors Khosla Ventures, Thrive Capital and Sequoia Capital

Abby Care is an AI-native home care startup that equips family caregivers with professional training, certification and ongoing support from dedicated RN care managers.  The company works with health plans to arrange care at home for families that need it. Abby Care's platform also gives care teams real-time visibility into care delivered in the home, helping ensure families receive the support they need while enabling health plans to verify that care is being provided. Fortune reported the series C round.

The U.S. faces a major healthcare workforce shortage along with a rapidly aging population, and waitlists of vulnerable children needing care, noted Havi Nguyen, founder of Abby Care in a LinkedIn post."Family caregivers already know their loved ones best and are in the home. They’re the first to notice when something isn’t right. At Abby, we equip family caregivers with training, AI, and support from our clinicians to deliver quality care. Our platform enables real-time capture of care data in the home. Health plans and states deserve visibility and confidence that care is delivered as intended. Better care and program integrity go together," Nguyen wrote.

Abby Care functions as a Medicaid provider to pay caregivers within Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Massachusetts, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Tennessee.

So far, Abby Care has helped families deliver millions of hours of care across many states, the company's members had 40%+ fewer reported hospitalizations in year one, she wrote.

Today, the company serves thousands of families across eight states, with additional markets expected to launch soon, executives said.

The funding will enable the company to bring its model to more families, deepen its work with health plans and continue building technology and clinical infrastructure, the company said in a blog post.

Oct. 14—AllswellBehavioral health for LGBTQ+Series: Seed Amount: $7 millionInvestors: Rethink Impact, Magnify Ventures, Ulu Ventures and Hopelab Ventures, Techstars and Amboy Street Ventures

Allswell offers one-on-one virtual therapy, group programs and trauma-informed care to LGBTQ+ patients. It is in-network with commercial and Medicaid payers. The startup, launched in 2025, plans to use the capital to expand beyond its DMV-area footprint, build out its clinical training program for therapists and launch psychiatric medication management next year.

"Nobody realizes how big this market is. Only 5% of Gen X identifies as LGBTQ+, compared with 25% of Gen Z. That's a massive generational and cultural shift, and we want to do for LGBTQ+ health what Midi did for menopause," Heidi Patel, managing partner at Rethink Impact, said in a press release.

Allswell's therapeutic models were built for patients navigating depression and anxiety, identity-specific trauma, family dynamics and social transition. It is also developing its own curriculum on PTSD and trauma care.

The startup, though new, is already seeing positive outcomes. The company often keeps patients for over a year, rare for behavioral health. In its most recent cohorts, 77% showed improvements in anxiety and 71% showed improvements in depression after 60 days of treatment.

"Our patients aren't used to being served with care and respect, or to having something built for them. ... This is a sleeping-giant category, and it has been underestimated at every step. Our ambition is to continue developing new, thoughtful clinical programs specifically for the LGBTQ+ community, regardless of the political climate," Dawn Androphy, co-founder and CEO of Allswell, said in an announcement.

Oct. 14—ReadilyArtificial intelligence compliance platformSeries: AAmount: $11 millionInvestors: Define Ventures led the funding round, with participation from Y Combinator and the California Health Care Foundation Innovation Fund.

Readily’s platform connects regulatory requirements with policies, assigned actions and supporting evidence to reduce manual research and review processes. When the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) releases new rules, CEO and co-founder Edward Tiong said, the platform can analyze them against existing policies and contracts “in hours,” identifying gaps and action items for teams.

The company’s work with healthcare organizations covers more than 25 million covered individuals across 46 states, according to its website. Tiong said revenue has grown 10x. Read the full story here.

Oct. 14—Probably GeneticAI platform powering the research, diagnosis and treatment of genetic diseasesSeries: AAmount: $12 millionInvestors: Round led by Threshold, with participation from Y Combinator and other existing investors.

The company’s primary product is a physician-ordered genetic test for undiagnosed rare disease patients, who typically face a seven-year diagnostic odyssey before getting answers. There are two pathways to testing: free testing, through pharma partnerships, and insurance-billed testing. The free programs address specific conditions, with a limited number of tests available at a time.

Patients can check their eligibility by completing a health and diagnostic assessment online. Probably Genetic’s AI platform converts self-reported symptoms, medical records and biological data into phenotypic data that it hopes can be used to train AI models for precision medicine in the future. Thus far, it has collected data from 130,000 patients.

Probably Genetic said the fresh funds would be used to grow the core part of the business, for hiring and to enter the drug discovery arena. Read the full story here.

Oct. 14—AllaraVirtual women’s health providerSeries: UndisclosedAmount: $30 millionInvestors: Led by Index Ventures and GV (Google Ventures), alongside new investors Camino Partners, Foreground and Family Fund.

Allara, founded in 2020, has expanded to serve a broader continuum of women’s health. The company aims to fill gaps in care for women often navigating an array of specialists. Each Allara patient is paired with a multidisciplinary team, including OB-GYNs, endocrinologists, registered dietitians and patient success leads.

Since its expansion nationwide last year, Allara has added urgent care visits for things like UTIs, bacterial vaginosis (BV) and STDs, and brought on more internal medicine providers to its interdisciplinary care team. It has also launched more supplements and medication delivery services.

The new funding will accelerate enterprise partnerships, expand Allara’s clinical infrastructure and support more AI features, executives said. Read the full story here.

Oct. 14—Confido HealthStartup building an agentic AI operating system Series: series A extensionAmount: $12.5 millionInvestors: Z47, formerly Matrix Partners India, led the extension round. Existing investors Together Fund and Blume Ventures also backed the series A extension.

Confido Health is expanding beyond AI voice agents to build out an agentic AI operating system that can execute administrative workflows across a medical practice.

The series A extension follows its $10 million series A round announced in September to continue scaling an AI platform for end-to-end healthcare operations.

Confido Health integrates with over 50 systems of record, including electronic health records, practice management systems, phone systems, billing systems and fax, without requiring any change to a practice's existing tech stack. Confido's AI agents can increase administrative staff's capacity to serve patients by automating routine tasks like appointment scheduling, insurance verification, billing and patient outreach, according to executives.

Confido Health executives assert that its agentic AI operations platform can actually execute administrative work across existing systems, helping practices increase capacity and control labor costs rather than simply giving staff another software tool.

Healthcare private equity veteran Justin Saks joined as an investor and board advisor. Read the full story here.

Oct. 13—SukiAmbient clinical intelligence Series: EAmount: $90 millionInvestors: Healthier Capital, Crosslink Capital and Hercules Capital. All existing institutional investors also backed the round, including Venrock, Flare Capital Partners, Hedosophia, Philips Ventures and Zoom Ventures.

Suki CEO and Founder Punit Soni told Fierce Healthcare the company is investing in three areas with the fresh capital: advancing its AI, expanding its commercial organization and scaling its partner ecosystem.

The company has raised more than $250 million to date, executives say. Patient encounters supported by its tools grew more than 190% year over year in 2026, with revenue doubling in 2025 and on track for similar growth this year.

Suki now works with over 250 healthcare organizations and more than 30 technology partners that embed its AI into their platforms, executives say. Read the full story here.

Oct. 8—OutroEvidence-informed medication tapering supportSeries: Pre-seed and seed Amount: $7 millionInvestors: Listen Ventures, Cake Ventures, Jason Calicanis’s LAUNCH, Actions Capital, Hannah Grey VC, SemperVirens, Brock Recovery Group, Pave Health Ventures, and more.

Outro aims to support safe deprescribing of medications, starting with antidepressants. The company combines specially-trained clinicians with evidence-informed tapering protocols, patient monitoring, psychosocial support and technology. Its program is available in 14 states.

"Deprescribing guidance has existed in countries like the U.K. for years," said Mark Horowitz, M.D., Ph.D., Outro's co-founder, psychiatry researcher and deprescribing expert, in an announcement. "Yet in America, where antidepressant use is widespread, tapering support is very hard to come by, so millions of patients are left without support when they are ready to come off."

The funding will support the growth of Outro’s deprescribing clinician network, further the application of AI to deprescribing-specific workflows, expand the company’s tapering model into additional drug classes and grow existing partnerships with leading universities and advocacy groups.

Earlier this year, the Department of Health & Human Services announced a plan to prevent the unnecessary initiation of psychiatric medications and support tapering and discontinuation for patients not experiencing clinical benefit. It recommended providers regularly review the risks and benefits of psychiatric medications and offer alternatives like therapy when clinically appropriate. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services also released guidance for providers on the importance of deprescribing.

Oct. 8—HealthleapClinical AI platform to flag undiagnosed conditionsSeries: seed/series AAmount: $38 millionInvestors: Sequoia Capital, First Round Capital and Hummingbird Ventures

Healthleap was founded by siblings Josiah and Jemima Meyer, who teamed up after Jemima, as a clinician, started building tools to help herself and colleagues treat patients faster, according to the company.

Launched in 2022, Healthleap aids hospitals in identifying undiagnosed conditions across inpatient and outpatient care settings. The company says its platform continuously analyzes every patient’s record, including notes, labs, vitals, orders, problem lists and flags risk for conditions. Healthleap then pushes actionable risk scores into optimized electronic health record workflows to support clinicians in identifying, treating and improving their patients’ health.

Healthleap has initially focused on disease-related malnutrition, a condition that costs the U.S. healthcare system up to $58 billion annually. The company says it is the first and only validated AI malnutrition screening tool that contains EHR-integrated screening layers. Read the full story here.

Oct. 7—General MedicineVirtual healthcare storefrontSeries: BAmount: $120 millionInvestors: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) led the round with participation from Matrix, VXI Capital, Eli Lilly and Company, Mercy Health through Granger Management and BoxGroup.

Startup General Medicine, started by the founding team that built PillPack and Amazon Pharmacy, is an online marketplace where customers can search, compare and buy care, see insurance and cash prices before deciding, and get guidance from a licensed clinician. The platform connects consumers to providers to either address specific medical needs or to chat about the symptoms they're having.

The company's platform connects healthcare recommendations to actual care, whether that means filling a prescription, ordering a lab test, scheduling a telehealth visit or booking an in-person appointment.

The company's executives refer to it as a "one-stop shop" for telemedicine, prescriptions, imaging, labs and specialists. Parker and PillPack co-founder Elliot Cohen teamed up with former Amazon executive Ashwin Muralidharan to get General Medicine off the ground in the fall of 2023. Read the full story here.

Oct. 6—VitalizeAI-powered operating system for staffing and schedulingSeries: AAmount: $31 millionInvestors: Oak HC/FT, Norwest Ventures, .406 Ventures, Constellation Ventures, Y Combinator and MemorialCare Innovation Fund.

Vitalize aims to supercharge health system capacity and operations with an artificial intelligence platform that unifies staffing, scheduling, flow and capacity.

At health systems, labor and capacity management are highly manual, inefficient processes that take up hours of administrative work each day.

Labor optimization is the key constraint behind patient flow, operational efficiency and financial performance across health systems, Veeraj Shah, co-founder and CEO of startup Vitalize, said. Capacity planning is the other half of the equation. Hospital revenue depends on matching patient demand to available beds and staff.

Vitalize founders view hospital staffing and capacity management as a complex logistics problem that directly affects finances, patient outcomes and clinician experience.

Vitalize positions its software as an "air traffic control" system for healthcare operations, helping health systems automate staffing, forecast demand, manage capacity and reduce reliance on overtime and agency labor, executives said. Vitalize’s AI automates the most manual scheduling tasks for clinical leaders, while forecasting demand and orchestrating staff across thousands of beds in real time. The company's platform uses machine learning, optimization models and AI agents to forecast staffing needs, fill schedule gaps, automate staffing workflows and recommend patient placement decisions, Shah noted. Read the full story here.

Oct. 1—Tiny HealthMicrobiome testing companySeries: BAmount: $33 millionInvestors: Capital B led the round, with participation from Spero Ventures, Black Opal Ventures, Pave Health Ventures, Alumni Ventures, Gaingels and others.

Tiny was launched in 2022, initially focusing on a microbiome test for babies and moms. "There was just a white space and nobody meeting the needs of those demographics,” Cheryl Sew Hoy, founder and CEO of Tiny Health, told Fierce Healthcare. Tiny expanded to a vaginal microbiome test, and today its adult tests have surpassed pediatric ones in volume.

The capital, which brings Tiny’s total raised to $46 million, will be used to advance research, expand provider education, scale the B2B platform and expand the patient-facing AI agent.

Alongside the funding news, Tiny announced the launch of a $5 million Microbiome Research Program to enable researchers, clinicians and scientific partners to investigate important intervention strategies in microbiome health. Read the full story here.

Sept. 29—EliseAIAI platform for housing and healthcareSeries: FAmount: $350 millionInvestors: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Bessemer Venture Partners led the financing, with participation from Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, Sapphire Ventures and Navitas Capital.

Artificial intelligence company EliseAI, which automates healthcare and housing systems, secured $350 million in financing Tuesday, reaching a $4 billion valuation.

EliseAI initially began as an AI company dedicated to automating communications in the rental and leasing industry, expanding into healthcare four years ago. It announced $250 million in series E funding last August.

The company said it surpassed $200 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) in June, doubling revenue year-over-year for five consecutive years. Its platform now powers one in six apartments, according to executives, and more than 30 million Americans have interacted with it since its launch.

“EliseAI has spent years building inside the day-to-day complexity of housing,” said Sameer Dholakia, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners partner, in a statement. “The company combines exceptional AI research and engineering with a detailed understanding of how properties operate. That depth has produced measurable results for their customers, leading to deep customer love.”

Earlier this month, the startup announced the launch of its first agentic AI teammate. The tool—dubbed Apollo—can perform any task in the Elise platform. Full story.

Sept. 24—Basalt Health AI layer for post-acute care admissionsSeries: AAmount: $20 millionInvestors: NEA led the round, with participation from Frist Cressey Ventures and 25m Health

Basalt Health uses AI to streamline post-acute care admissions. The company plans to use the capital to expand its platform and grow its team.

Basalt's technology automates the referral and admissions process for post-acute providers, analyzing incoming referrals from faxes, portals and EHR integrations and matching patients to appropriate facilities based on clinical and payer criteria. The company says its platform reduces administrative work and speeds placement decisions that are often delayed by manual processes.

Each year, roughly 14 million patients enter post-acute care—yet the placement process has failed to evolve. The archaic process typically involves case managers faxing lengthy clinical packets to 6.6 facilities per placement, then waiting for the right bed to respond. The resulting delays and mismatches contribute to an estimated $17 billion in avoidable readmission costs annually.

After nearly a decade at Accolade, where he saw administrative work increasingly pull clinicians away from patients, Ben Hackett founded Basalt in 2024 to build technology that fits existing workflows, reduces friction and gives care teams more time to focus on patients.

The startup reports strong early traction with major health systems. Basalt has been live with Lifepoint Health’s team since its seed round in 2025 and the company has reduced median chart processing time from 8.5 minutes to 1.2 minutes. Basalt is also being implemented across 49 additional Lifepoint markets by the end of 2026.

“Case managers are still sending 70-page packets and waiting for responses, while patients remain stranded in hospital beds,” Hackett, founder and CEO of Basalt Health, said. “Basalt turns that uncertainty into fast, defensible decisions. This funding gives us the power to transform one of healthcare’s most stubbornly inefficient systems.”

Basalt plans to expand beyond admissions into discharge planning and payer workflows, positioning its AI platform as infrastructure for managing patient transitions into post-acute care.

Sept. 24—RightwayPharmacy benefit management and care navigation Series: EAmount: $155 millionInvestors: Francisco Partners led the round, with participation from existing investors Thrive Capital and Khosla Venture

Rightway plans to use the fresh capital to expand its AI capabilities and pharmacy benefits technology platform.

Rightway positions itself as an alternative to traditional pharmacy benefit managers by aligning its financial incentives with employers' goal of reducing drug costs. The company says it now serves 45 Fortune 500 clients and offers a model that combines pharmacist-led clinical guidance, care navigation services and transparent pharmacy pricing. The company says its SureSpend model includes a pharmacy spending cap and passes through 100% of rebates, including for high-cost drug categories such as GLP-1s.

Jordan Feldman, Rightway's co-founder and CEO said, "We built our financial model to reward getting members onto high-value drugs, and we embedded clinicians in the workflow and AI on the backend to do it. If we can help employers get more from one of their largest and fastest-growing healthcare expenses, we make healthcare more affordable for companies and the people who work for them."

Rightway will use the Series E financing to expand its AI capabilities and the technology that powers its pharmacy benefits model. "The pharmacy supply chain carries a lot of cost that has nothing to do with the medication itself," Feldman said. "Our technology and AI pull costs out of a bloated ecosystem that has failed to be efficient and transparent. That combination of better economics, better technology, and human clinical expertise means better care for members and lower costs for employers."

Sept. 22—HeidiAI clinical assistantSeries: series C and growth investment Amount: $100 million series C and $240 million growth investmentInvestors: Blackbird led Heidi's $100 million series C funding, which was also backed by existing investors including Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline. General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund provided the $240 million growth investment l

Healthcare startup Heidi will use the funding to push beyond clinical documentation into AI-powered workflow automation and agentic capabilities for clinicians.

The company, which first launched in Australia, initially started as an ambient AI medical scribe and then expanded into point-of-care clinical guidelines with Heidi Evidence and AI hardware (Remote) for clinical work as well as a voice-to-text feature, called Dictate.

Heidi says it now supports around 2.8 million patient interactions each week in 110 languages from 190 countries.

Heidi will use the funding to expand its capabilities beyond the visit, moving from documentation into supervised action and giving clinicians more time back for patients. Full story

Sept. 22—Blair HealthAugmenting generalist careSeries: pre-seedAmount: $4.24 million Canadian dollarsInvestors: Business Development Bank of Canada’s Thrive Venture Fund, Accelia Capital, Ogaei Investments, Ontario Centre of Innovation and angel investors

Blair Health, a clinical infrastructure company and virtual provider, plans to expand across Canada and the U.S. It is currently in seven states, available DTC and through employers.

Blair enables generalist providers to deliver specialty care. It is built with medical specialists, encoding their assessment logic, protocols, escalation triggers and follow-up pathways into its software. This then enables Blair’s in-house NPs and family docs to deliver specialty care, with subspecialists providing oversight and support for complex cases.

A patient may come in with complex symptoms that typically take several visits and a waiting list for a specialist to address. But Blair can treat them right away, it says, with the patient completing a structured intake modeled on a specialty clinic assessment. Then, Blair's LLM provides the family doc a recommended treatment plan. The doc reviews, adjusts and prescribes as needed.

“The clinician always makes the final decision; Blair gives them specialist-level structure to do it,” Madge Rumman, Blair co-founder and CEO, told Fierce Healthcare over email.

When a patient needs prescriptions, labs or other in-person services, Blair coordinates with those providers accordingly. Blair currently offers care across menopause, urology, pelvic health, clinical nutrition and weight management.

Sept. 18—Penelope Health Provider and payer policy intelligence platformSeries: undisclosedAmount: $100 millionInvestors: Thoreau

The company aggregates and standardizes insurer coverage policies, prior authorization requirements, medical necessity criteria and coding rules, giving providers and healthcare organizations real-time access to payer requirements before care is delivered. Penelope says its platform currently covers policies affecting more than 200 million Americans and over 15,000 procedures and drug codes.

The new funding will help Penelope expand coverage to more insurers and policy types, develop new products, build infrastructure that moves coverage determination and policy intelligence upstream to the point of care and create a shared infrastructure layer for real-time payments and clinical rules that can be used across healthcare systems.

Sept.10—Epsilon HealthPrecision healthcare AISeries: stealthAmount: $27.6 millionInvestors: AlleyCorp, with participation from Uncork Capital, Renegade Partners, SemperVirens, and Jack Altman.

AI-native radiology practice Epsilon Health emerged from stealth to speed up medical imaging interpretation.

Epsilon’s model combines AI with physician oversight to accelerate clinical workflows while reducing administrative burden.

The funding will accelerate Epsilon’s market expansion and support practices through hiring, expanded clinical partnerships and new infrastructure investments.

“Epsilon has built an entirely new kind of radiology practice, which I think makes a great blueprint for how healthcare will be done in the future,” said Jack Altman, who previously invested through Alt Capital, in a statement. “In less than 10 months, they’ve gone from nothing to processing thousands of studies a day for some of the largest imaging providers in the country. I couldn’t be more excited about what they’re doing.”

Sept. 9—VivPatented tampon technologySeries: undisclosedAmount: $2 millionInvestors: Launchpad Venture Group, Shelly Berkowitz of SSB Next Chapter Holdings, Westchester Angels and individual investors

Period care brand Viv is continuing its expansion across the U.S.

The company is built on toxin-free products and will use recently announced funding for its nationwide launch into Whole Foods markets and rollout of its Cottonlock tampons.

“Since starting Viv, making products with the highest quality of care has been our guiding principle,” said Katie Diasti, Viv co-founder and CEO, in a statement. “When we saw the research revealing how harmful fibers are left behind from tampons - even premium organic ones - we had to find a solution to continue offering women products that would support their health – no exceptions. Discovering the difference between a tampon with a protective veil and without was eye-opening, and we knew we had to act fast to bring a new product with this technology to market. We’re excited to be the first tampon with this technology and to continue setting the bar higher for quality menstrual care. Women deserve the best.”

Viv has raised $3.3 million to date, the company says.

Sept. 9—VerilyPrecision healthcare AISeries: undisclosedAmount: undisclosedInvestors: NVIDIA, with participation from existing investor CU Healthcare Innovation Fund II, LP.

Verily announced new investments from NVIDIA and CU Healthcare Innovation Fund, as it extends its March fundraising.

The funding comes as it scales adoption of its flagship data and AI platform—Verily Pre Platform—which aids healthcare organizations in deploying AI responsibly and ensuring data is AI-ready. The funds will also support its patient engagement offering Verily Me.

“We are pleased to welcome NVIDIA as a new investor in Verily. These investments strengthen our ability to pursue the opportunity ahead,” said Stephen Gillett, Verily CEO and chairman, in a statement. “Together, these investments and the continued support of our current investors accelerate our vision to build a trusted foundation for healthcare, bringing together the information and intelligence needed to power better decisions and unlock the full potential of AI across the healthcare ecosystem.”

Sept. 9—ImplicityAI-driven cardiac monitoring platformSeries: undisclosedAmount: $40 millionInvestors: IRIS, with participation from Five Arrows

AI-driven cardiac monitoring company Implicity is scaling its platform globally.

Implicity’s platform is a single solution for cardiac monitoring that aggregates, normalizes and analyzes data across the full care continuum regardless of manufacturer. Moreover, it integrates directly into electronic health records (EHRs).

It plans to use the funding round to expand further into the U.S. through local hires, build on established European leadership and invest further in AI.

The company serves more than 250 medical centers, monitoring more than 120,000 patients daily across the U.S., France and Germany.

“I didn't become a physician to manage data — I became one to treat patients,” said Arnaud Rosier, M.D., Ph.D., Implicity co-founder and CEO, in a statement. “This funding lets us care for patients at scale, catching the information through the noise to provide the best possible care — and that's the future of cardiology I've been chasing since my first year as an electrophysiologist.”

Sept. 8—GenHealth.aiAI-powered back office agentsSeries: AAmount: $16.5 millionInvestors: Flare Capital Partners, with participation from existing investors Craft Ventures and Obvious Ventures and new investors Eniac Ventures, InHealth Ventures, Epsilon Health Investors and ARTIS

Startup GenHealth.ai deploys its agents into provider offices to reduce administrative burden.

Founded in 2023, GenHealth.ai’s tools complete revenue cycle workflows end-to-end across electronic health records (EHRs), payer portals and other systems and can handle intake, eligibility, prior authorizations, billing and denials.

“The problem with automating healthcare administration isn’t just the AI—it’s that the AI is disconnected from the workflows and systems providers already use, like EHRs, payer portals, fax and bank accounts,” said Ricky Sahu, GenHealth.ai CEO, in a statement. “At GenHealth, we've built these connections directly and created the infrastructure for AI agents to execute complex workflows reliably, with additional context from our own model trained on data from 140 million patients. The result is patients getting care faster and providers getting paid over 30% more. That outcome is virtually unheard of in RCM.”

GenHealth.ai has raised $30 million to date, executives say. Full story.

Sept. 8—ForusAI-powered medication access platformSeries: CAmount: $150 millionInvestors: Bain Capital Ventures, with participation from existing investors including Thrive Capital, General Catalyst, Accel, Redpoint, BoxGroup, Pear VC, Vast Ventures and SV Angel

Health tech startup Forus automates prescription workflows with AI, and plans to expand its network with its latest funding round into more medical specialties and care settings.

The company, which launched three years ago, says it now has nationwide reach and is used by thousands of medical practices and health systems in all 50 states. Forus now supports patients in 85% of U.S. residential zip codes, including many with complex conditions, executives say.

The fresh funding comes just four months after the company announced it raised $160 million in a series B round. The latest funding round boosts Forus' valuation to $3 billion. Full story.

Sept. 2—Scan.comU.S. medical imaging networkSeries: C, debt facilities fundingAmount: $220 millionInvestors: Noteus Partners, with participation from Aviva, Concord Health Partners, YZR Capital, Oxford Capital and more. Debt facilities provided by VerisFi Capital and Atempo Growth

Medical imaging platform Scan.com plans to build the largest medical imaging network in the U.S.

Launched in the U.K in 2017, the company connects payers, providers and patients to imaging centers. Its platform connects search, scheduling and results delivery for imaging into a single national API, integrating live and two-way with independent imaging centers' own scheduling systems and electronic medical records (EMRs). It expanded into the U.S. in 2023.

More than 900,000 patients have used the network for care globally to date, according to the company. Scan.com says revenue has doubled over the past year to surpass a $165 million annualized run rate.

The company plans to use the funding to further expand its U.S. network of imaging providers as well as invest in its API and agentic AI infrastructure. Full story.

Sept. 2—Thyme CareValue-based oncology care companySeries: EAmount: $125 millionInvestors: JPMorgan's Morgan Health, with participation from strategic investors including Humana and CVS Health Ventures

Oncology company Thyme Care is planning to expand its offerings to address broader cancer care challenges.

Through a recently announced series E funding round, it plans to establish a new parent organization named Thyme Companies. Thyme Care remains the anchor of the Thyme Companies family of businesses; its name, partnerships and member experience remain unchanged, the company said.

The newly formed Thyme Companies will develop a portfolio of new, independent businesses that address persistent barriers to improved cancer care. Areas under active development include accelerating the adoption of lower-cost biosimilars and improving clinical trial accrual.

Thyme Care’s services are now available to 10.5 million people nationwide and the company manages more than $7 billion in oncology spending, executives say. Full story.

August 26—ArintraAI-driven revenue assuranceSeries: BAmount: $25 millionInvestors: Define Ventures, with participation from existing investors including Peak XV Partners, YNHH Center for Health Care Innovation, Endeavor Health Ventures, Y Combinator, Counterpart Ventures, Ten13 and Spider Capital

Artificial intelligence-driven medical coding platform Arintra announced Wednesday it is expanding its revenue cycle platform.

Arintra co-founder and CEO Nitesh Shroff told Fierce Healthcare the company plans to use the capital to broaden its revenue assurance platform, expand across more enterprise health systems and expand its clinical and specialty coverage.

Launched in 2020, the platform codes charts at scale to reveal patterns related to documentation, outcomes, work relative value units (wRVUs) and denials. It says its revenue assurance platform is the first of its kind, unifying revenue cycle management (RCM) operations. Arintra executives say its approach provides customers with a 5.1% increase in compliant revenue capture, a 32% reduction in cost and a 43% decrease in coding-related denials.

Arintra has raised $51 million to date, according to Shroff. Full story.

August 25—OmicsBankClinical data infrastructureSeries: seedAmount: $2.25 millionInvestors: Redesign Health

Clinical data infrastructure company OmicsBank plans to use the funding to support its expansion into U.S. markets and continue to grow its clinical data network across Asia and the Middle East.

Founded in 2025, the company's technology is currently in more than 90 hospitals and diagnostic labs in Asia. Its clinical dataset includes longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data from 12.5 million patients, more than 30 million DICOM images, 6 million pathology slides and 500,000 genome sequences, executives say.

Alongside planned expansion, OmicsBank is also developing GPU-enabled research environments for AI model training, reinforcement learning environments, biomarker discovery and more.

"Drug development and healthcare AI are becoming increasingly sophisticated, but the data powering them still represents a relatively narrow slice of the world," said Sumit Sinha, OmicsBank CEO and co-founder, in a statement. "We've built the infrastructure to make rich clinical and biological data from Asia and other underrepresented populations available for research, ethically and at scale, while remaining compliant with local and international laws. As we expand beyond Asia, including the U.S., we see an opportunity to connect that global data foundation with leading health systems, drug developers, and AI companies to build a much richer picture of human health."

August 20—MaxQ MedicalProstate care platformSeries: AAmount: $31.5 millionInvestors: Atlantic Blue Ventures, S3 Ventures, and Olympus Innovation Ventures led the round, with participation from existing investor Hillside Capital.

Private health tech company MaxQ Medical is developing an all-in-one transurethral imaging and therapy system for prostate care.

The system its developing combines advanced imaging with tissue-selective therapy in a single transurethral procedure in an effort to minimize side effects and preserve the urethra. MaxQ Medical's first indication is benign prostate hyperplasia (BPH), with plans to expand into focal therapy for prostate cancer and eventually into broader prostate diagnostics.

It plans to use the funding round to grow its team and advance its clinical program.

MaxQ Medical CEO Amir Tehrani said in a statement the system is designed to "offer the durability of gold standard resective therapies with side-effects more comparable to tMIS solutions."

"I want to thank our investors for their support, our exceptional team for their dedication, and Amir Abolfathi, our executive chairman, co-leading this financing effort with me," Tehrani said. "This funding lets us continue the clinical evaluations already underway and move closer to giving physicians and their patients a better option."

August 18—HopscotchTech-enabled provider focused on rural regionsSeries: DAmount: $53 millionInvestors: 8VC and Townhall Ventures led the round, with participation from a slew of investors, including Citi Impact Fund, Alumni Ventures, K2 HealthVentures and the Autism Impact Fund

Hopscotch Primary Care plans to use the funds to expand beyond its current core market in Western North Carolina, likely to Tennessee and Georgia. Across its dozen clinics, Hopscotch offers longer primary care appointments, between 20 and 40 minutes, and leverages ambient scribes to generate visit and patient instruction summaries. It also uses AI-driven clinical decision support tools to help clinicians manage complex patients. Telehealth is an option, with some encounters offered in-house and some outsourced to provider partners who offer virtual specialty care.

When it comes to patients, Hopscotch often sees complex seniors, which is why it focuses on advanced primary care. It accepts Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid and commercial plans.

The company was founded in 2021 and has served over 15,000 patients to date. Full story

August 18—Happy HealthAI-powered platform for continuous home-based careSeries: AAmount: $75 millionInvestors: ARCH Venture Partners and OpenLoop led the funding

Digital health company Happy Health secured fresh funding to continue building its artificial intelligence-powered platform for continuous home-based care.

The Austin, Texas-based startup’s first application focuses on sleep because it “offers one of the richest windows into human physiology,” executives say. Its clinical-grade smart ring—dubbed Happy Ring—first received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval in October 2024.

Happy Sleep—the company’s comprehensive sleep medicine platform—also includes a clinical care team comprised of board-certified sleep physicians. The company’s website says it is in-network with most major health insurance plans, including Blue Cross and Medicare.

The Happy Ring was later approved for at-home sleep testing in June 2025, making it the first FDA-cleared smart ring for multi-night sleep testing and 24/7 biometrics. Full story

August 13—Aligned MarketplaceConnecting self-insured employers to primary careSeries: AAmount: $20 millionInvestors: Led by Venrock,

Aligned Marketplace runs a marketplace that connects self-insured employers and third party administrators to independent advanced and direct primary care and specialty care providers. The funding will be used to expand access to independent primary care practices, and the company is expanding its marketplace to include value-based specialty care. With more than 3,000 in-person clinics across all 50 states, Aligned sits atop employers’ existing carrier or third-party administrator.

Aligned Marketplace says it has experienced tremendous growth and cost savings for its employer customers over the past 18 months, having achieved measurable outcomes with large Fortune 500 employers.

In a program launched on January 1, 2025, engaged members at a Fortune 500 company with a national footprint cost 12% less than a risk-matched national benchmark built by a third-party actuarial firm, a savings of $96 per member per month, according to the company. Members at the same company who did not engage with an Aligned doctor came in at benchmark. The company says 70% of engaged members were identified as high risk, and those members moved their care toward their Aligned doctor, averaging 4.7 visits with that doctor and 1.6 fewer visits elsewhere.  More time with a primary care doctor showed up in preventative care, with engaged members roughly doubling their mammogram rate and nearly tripling their colonoscopy rate after their first visit.

“Our mission is to increase America’s healthy years. Unfortunately, the healthcare system was built to treat illness and generate volume, not to keep people healthy, control costs for the employer who pays the bills, or let independent doctors practice the way they want. We’ve proven that a different model works — one where keeping people healthy actually saves money,” said Patrick Nelli, founder and CEO of Aligned Marketplace in a statement. Press release

August 11—Flagler Health AI-native operating system for musculoskeletal careSeries: BAmount: $50 millionInvestors: Bessemer Venture Partners led the funding round, with participation from SignalFire, Alumni Ventures, Streamlined, 186 Ventures, Proof VC, Tribeca Ventures and Offscript

Flagler Health banked funding to continue building out its AI-native operating system for musculoskeletal (MSK) care. The company says its platform is trained on one of the largest MSK patient datasets and integrates directly into existing electronic medical records (EMRs) and workflows. The platform orchestrates the full patient lifecycle, across triage, care management, billing and patient communications, turning manual, reactive clinics into coordinated, data-driven operations, according to executives.

The AI-native platform has scaled to thousands of MSK providers across more than 36 states, and executives say it generates an average of $164,000 in additional annual revenue per provider. Moreover, 87% of patients report improvement in pain, mood, sleep or mobility. Full story

August 6—HealthSnap AI-powered virtual care managementAmount: $25 millionInvestors: Eastward Capital Partners

HealthSnap secured a growth financing facility to strengthen its balance sheet and refinance existing debt. The funding also provides significant additional capital to accelerate artificial intelligence innovation, expand commercial operations, and scale deployment of its Advanced Primary Care Management (APCM) platform across health systems, the company said.

HealthSnap brings together remote patient monitoring, chronic care management, principal care management, advanced primary care management, AI-powered clinical workflows, enterprise analytics, reimbursement optimization and care coordination into a single, EMR-Integrated, intelligent platform. Healthcare organizations use the platform to proactively manage patients at scale, unlocking capacity without adding headcount, the company said.

HealthSnap supports more than 80,000 active patient programs across 200 health systems and physician organizations, with the company projecting more than 100,000 active patient programs by the end of 2026. HealthSnap's platform currently ingests two patient measurements every second and patients enrolled in HealthSnap's programs see a 97% reduction in alert frequency by their 12th month, demonstrating remote patient management at scale.

The company is also expanding the use of AI agents to support routine patient interactions, including enrollment, device troubleshooting, and compliance outreach, allowing care teams to focus their time and expertise where they matter most. The new financing will accelerate deployment of next-generation AI capabilities while supporting continued investment in product innovation, engineering, commercial expansion, customer success and enterprise growth, executives said. News release

July 28—Throne ScienceSmart toilet sensorSeries: AAmount: $10 millionInvestors: Will Ventures led the round with participation from Emerson Collective, Workshop, LEAD VC, Salt VC, Accomplice, Moxxie, Ventures Together, Symphony, Felix Capital, Cosmic Venture Partners, Offscript, V1.VC, and Morrison Seger

Throne Science is flush with cash after raising a series A round to expand its team and invest in R&D efforts for the next generation of its smart toilet sensor device that tracks gut health, hydration and urinary function. Throne was founded in 2023 and launched to consumers in March 2026. The device attaches to any standard toilet and uses computer vision and AI to track bathroom habits, provide personalized health insights and establish patterns around gut health and hydration over time.

Throne is establishing itself as the premier gut-health wearable for both everyday users and the 25–45 million Americans living with conditions like IBS. Earlier in July, Throne launched the beta version of its Gut Health AI coach, a highly requested feature that enables users to ask questions about their gut health data and receive personalized feedback.

The company has made key leadership hires from the consumer wearable and health tech industries. Ben Grynol, formerly head of growth at Levels Health, joined the company as VP of Growth, David Strasfeld, Ph.D., joined as SVP of R&D having previously served as VP of research and innovation at Lumicell and co-founder of Precision Healing. Karan Rajan, M.D., a NHS surgeon, educator and author with a large following on social media, joined the company as chief of science.

“We live in an age where tracking steps, heart rate, sleep, and recovery has become the norm, and yet we disregard the vital insights that come with our bowel movements,” said Throne CEO and founder, Scott Hickle in a statement. “Throne is building a platform that will not only provide valuable data about gut health and hydration, but in future iterations of the technology, will also sound alarms regarding more serious health conditions. This raise is an important stepping stone to build the infrastructure we need to get to the next level." Press release

July 16—Bunkerhill Health Agentic AI platform for health systemsSeries: BAmount: $25 million ($55 million total raised including seed and series A)Investors: Led by Khosla Ventures, with continued participation from Sequoia Capital, Felicis, Optum Ventures and Y Combinator

Bunkerhill Health announced a series B round of fundraising on July 16, bringing the company's total fundraising to $55 million, including two previous rounds. The series B round was $25 million.

“Medicine has advanced faster than our healthcare system's ability to operationalize it,” said Nishith Khandwala, co-founder and chief executive officer of Bunkerhill Health, in a statement. “Every leading health system has more opportunities to improve patient outcomes than its workforce has capacity to address. We believe AI agents can help them turn more of those ideas into reality.”

The company's platform, Carebricks, allows hospitals and health systems to transform ideas into AI agents across multiple domains. Currently, Carebricks is utilized by major health platforms, such as Cleveland Clinic, the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) and Intermountain Health.

Bunkerhill Health intends to use this funding to expand its Carebricks platform, helping health systems turn a wider range of their own clinical and operational ideas into production-grade AI agents while advancing the governance, monitoring and safeguards that health systems require to deploy AI at scale.

July 15—RimeEnterprise voice AI platform that builds conversational speech models Series: AAmount: $24 millionInvestors: Led by M13, with participation from Twilio Ventures, Corazon Capital, and continued participation from Unusual Ventures and other existing investors

Rime takes a linguistics-first approach to develop conversational speech models, powering nearly 100 million phone calls monthly for global leaders like Mayo Clinic, Dialpad, Upstart and Asurion.

Founded by Lily Clifford (while pursuing a Stanford linguistics Ph.D.), Brooke Larson (Ph.D. linguist, ex-Amazon Alexa), and Ares Geovanis (Stanford engineer), Rime has gained traction for its ability to keep customers on the line longer, according to a recent study by Miravoice.

As part of these recent investments, Morgan Blumberg, partner at M13, will join Rime’s board of directors. Rafael Valle will also join Rime as Chief Science Officer from Meta’s Super Intelligence Lab. Rime intends to use the funds to invest in its conversational dataset and strategically hire in engineering and research.

"The design patterns that will define the speech-to-speech era of AI haven't been built yet. Rime is doing the foundational work by combining frontier AI with deep linguistic expertise to create the speech infrastructure the next generation of AI products will rely on,” Blumberg said in a statement.

July 15—Neko HealthTech-enabled preventive health and non-invasive diagnostic scansSeries: CAmount: $700 millionInvestors: Lightspeed Venture Partners and O.G. Venture Partners co-led the series C round, with participation from existing investors Atomico, General Catalyst and Lakestar, alongside new backers including Liberty City Ventures, Positive Sum and BDT & MSD. The funding round also saw participation from a list of individuals and celebrities.

Tech-enabled preventive health startup Neko Health banked $700 million to break into the U.S. market with plans to open a New York City clinic later this year. The company, founded by Daniel Ek, the founder and former CEO of Spotify, and Hjalmar Nilsonne, offers non-invasive, radiation-free diagnostic scans that it says captures millions of health data points. See full story.

July 13—Corner Health AI-native practice operating system to help build provider-owned primary care clinicsSeries: AAmount: $32.5 millionInvestors: Led by Oak HC/FT, with participation from existing investors First Round Capital and Zigg Capital

Corner Health intends to reinvigorate the healthcare system by empowering nurse practitioners to start and scale their own local primary care practices.

The startup's newly developed AI technology, Cora, automates primary care operations, including scheduling, patient communication, billing, lab orders, referrals and prior authorizations. As a result of this technological advancement, 90% of Corner Health clinics operate with no additional staff, which reduces overhead and gives NPs more time to focus on patients.

Co-founders Lava Sunder and Anne Gifford intend to use the funding to continue to scale Corner Health during a period of rapid growth. The company established a network of more than 70 provider-owned primary care practices. Corner Health is the fastest-growing primary care network in Arizona and Washington and has enabled more than 35,000 patient visits in the past year.

"The dominant use of AI in healthcare today is helping clinicians move faster and see more patients," Gifford, who serves as chief operating officer, said in a statement. "We're using AI to create the opposite outcome. Our providers can see fewer patients, spend 2-3x more time with each one, and still build thriving independent practices."

July 15—TytoCareAI-enabled remote physical examination technology provider Series: growth roundAmount: $25 millionInvestors: Led by Insight Partners along with HOOP, OliveTree, OrbiMed, Qumra Capital, Qualcomm Ventures and others

TytoCare, a handheld examination platform featuring FDA-cleared medical devices and a suite of AI-powered SaMD (software as a medical device) algorithms, closed a closing of a $25 million-plus growth round. The company also appointed Adam Pellegrini as CEO, who has over two decades of experience in digital health.

These significant announcements come as TytoCare moves to embed its remote examination platform and SaMD algorithms directly into integrated care pathways for remote cardiopulmonary monitoring, oncology support and complex chronic disease management, disease areas where the gap between in-person clinical rigor and virtual care delivery has remained wide.

More specifically, the proceeds from the financing round will fund expansion of the company’s AI clinical algorithms pipeline, deepening of payer and health system partnerships and acceleration of go-to-market efforts targeting chronic and serious disease populations, the company said.

“The convergence of a clinically validated exam device, AI-powered diagnostic algorithms, and the urgent demand from health systems for real clinical intelligence at the point of virtual care is an extraordinary and rare combination,” Pellegrini said in statement. “TytoCare has built the foundational infrastructure for the next generation of intelligent remote care, and I could not be more energized to lead this next chapter.”

July 8—Pearl HealthTech and AI for Medicare providersSeries: CAmount: $110 million in an equity and debt financing package, including a $50 million series CInvestors:

Health tech startup Pearl Health raised $110 million in a mix of debt and equity financing to build out its artificial intelligence platform for Medicare providers, including AI agents to handle administrative tasks.

The company, which launched in November 2020, provides technology to help providers deliver preemptive care to Medicare patients through AI-powered predictive insights, financial risk modeling and streamlined workflows. Pearl says it supports a network of over 10,000 providers, including health systems such as University of Vermont Health and MDX Hawaii, across more than 40 states, caring for over 250,000 Medicare beneficiaries. See full story

June 25—EvidencedVC firm focused on regulation-conscious health technologySeries: Fund IAmount: $24 millionInvestors: Rockefeller Foundation, the RockCreek Group and Colibri Equity Ventures, alongside undisclosed individual LPs.

Evidenced gets its namesake from the idea that good investing requires decisions based on the best available evidence. The firm was founded in 2022 by Bryan Sivak and Sean Glass, who see regulation and policy as a catalyst for new market opportunities, rather than risk.

Sivak was previously CTO at HHS under President Obama. Glass co-founded Advantia Health, a women's healthcare company. Policies they see as opportunities include the CMS ACCESS model and the Rural Health Transformation Fund.

Evidence backs early-stage companies. Thus far, it has invested in Floreo, Ilant Health, Koda Health and Photon Health, among others. Their portfolio is described more in depth on their Substack.

While acknowledging the challenge of raising money as an emerging fund, Glass has also highlighted his belief in a smaller fund's ability to raise solid returns for investors. "As the fund gets bigger, it gets very hard to produce a very high IRR for your LPs, because the number of mega-exits you have to have is just highly unlikely," Glass told Health Tech Nerds.

June 25—TraseControlled AI agent platformSeries: SeedAmount: $107 millionInvestors: Led by ARCH Venture Partners with participation from Red Cell Partners and others.

Trase is an AI solutions platform that offers operating systems and agents for high-stakes environments.

In the healthcare space, Trase has been working alongside Duke University Health System to deploy specialized agents within its Division of Cardiology. The health system has used Trase's technology to automate the more than 5,000 faxes the clinic receives each month, which unlocked $285,450 in annual staff capacity, with those hours reinvested in patient care, not headcount reduction, the organization said. Trase’s fax routing agent is not the only one employed at Duke, however, other models have tackled time-consuming administrative workflows and managed chronic conditions.

Trase intends to use the funds to expand its go-to-market team and continue developing the company’s operating systems. "In the age of AI, powered by the sovereignty, predictability, and trustworthiness that Trase’s OS delivers, agents are handling the onerous, immutable tasks that bog down highly trained individuals. Shifting that valuable mental capacity to higher-acuity work will help make the most important systems in the United States cheaper, faster, and better for every American," Grant Verstandig, CEO and co-founder of Trase, said.

June 24—XCuresClinical clarity engine for patient recordsSeries: BAmount: $46 millionInvestors: Led by Innovius Capital, with participation from iGrow, GKCC, Spring Mountain Capitall and existing investors.

xCures is a healthcare AI data processor and creator of the clinical clarity engine, which transforms fragmented patient records into decision-ready data in minutes. Given that 80% of healthcare data is unstructured, the company's clinical clarity engine seeks to improve healthcare outcomes by structuring this data, XCures executives said.

As it stands, xCures has processed over 300 million patient records from more than 550,000 locations across the U.S. This new funding brings the startup's total funding to more than $76 million, and the company's aim is to continue to expand its clinical data engine.

"Healthcare has spent decades generating enormous amounts of patient data without a reliable way to make that information usable. We're changing that," said Mika Newton, CEO of xCures. "This financing allows us to accelerate product development, expand our team, and help more organizations turn fragmented records into information they can actually act on."

June 17—Clair HealthHormone monitor for womenSeries: SeedAmount: $11.6 millionInvestors: Led by Khosla Ventures, with support from a16z speedrun, Brydge Club, Treehub, Cartan Capital, AGI House, Insiders VC, Anne Wojcicki and other investors

Clair is a jewelry-inspired wrist device that is built specifically to monitor women’s hormones by utilizing 10 biosensors and more than 130 proprietary biomarkers. It is designed to offer a non-invasive alternative to traditional hormone monitoring methods for estrogen, progesterone, LH and FSH. Clair Health was designed to provide a holistic understanding of health, by tracking fertility, aligning fitness routines with hormonal phases and offering information about cycle irregularities, the company said.

Clair Health executives said in a press release that the health monitor aims to fill an existing gap in the market, as many wearable healthcare technologies currently prioritize male physiology with women’s health as an afterthought. Founded by recent Stanford graduates Jenny Duan and Abhinav Agarwal, Clair will directly address the women’s health funding and research gap. They intend to use the funding to assist with the launch of Clair’s wearable bracelet and app in November 2026.

"Wearables are great at monitoring metrics like HRV, sleep step count, and breathing rate," Duan said in a statement. "They use biosensors and AI to infer those metrics, without directly measuring them. What they’ve missed is that all of these signals for women are being shaped by their hormones. The data has always been there; we just haven't had something to read it until now. What we’re building will shape how we interpret women’s health and support the overall wellbeing of women."

June 4—ScispotAI operator for laboratory scienceSeries: AAmount: $8 millionInvestors: Led by Avenue Growth Partners

Scispot is a Canadian company that supports modern labs across biotech, pharma, diagnostics, genomics, CRO/CDMO, bioproduction, biobanking and testing workflows through their AI-native operations system. Currently, Scispot is utilized by 100+ labs, supporting 250+ instrument types, 1000+ experiments per month, and millions of samples, according to the company’s statement. Their platform aims to transform daily laboratory work into data sets that can be used by teams of scientists and AI.

Modern labs remain under significant pressure to adapt to an increasingly AI native world, which is something Scispot seeks to address. While maintaining human judgement, their platform allows for digital work to be automated in a move towards more efficient, and eventually “self-driving” laboratories. A self-driving lab is defined by the company as “a lab where routine coordination, data capture, analysis, and reporting run automatically on an operating layer built for traceability, human review, and control.”

The press release emphasized Scispot’s Canadian roots, with the funding round focused on adding high-skill roles to their headquarters in Kitchener-Waterloo, Ontario, specifically in their product, engineering, AI, implementation and customer success teams.

Brian Goldsmith, a founding partner at Avenue Growth, said, "The life sciences AI stack needs more than compute and models. It needs an execution layer that turns physical lab work into structured, traceable context. Scispot gives labs that layer, so AI agents can support real lab work with traceability and control."

June 3—LassieAI to run doctors' officesSeries: AAmount: $35 millionInvestors: Led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with support from Night Capital, Rahul Vohra, founder and former CEO of Superhuman; Zach Perret, co-founder and CEO of Plaid; Taavet Hinrikus, co-founder and former CEO of Wise; Gokul Rajaram; and Brian Balfour, co-founder and CEO of Reforge.

Lassie will do doctors' paperwork as the startup built autonomous systems to run small businesses Lassie’s AI agent is currently supports 700 practices across 49 states, and teh company claims its AI saves health practices over 250,000 hours of labor each year.

A typical practice loses more than 100 hours a month to administrative work and spends roughly $200,000 a year on staff that owners can barely find, let alone keep, according to the startup.

Lassie’s AI agent goes into a practice's insurance portals, pulls reimbursements, reconciles them against records, updates the system-of-record and verifies the funds in the bank, the company said.

Lassie was founded by Steijn Pelle, an early product manager at Robinhood and Coinbase, and Frédéric Renken, the first product hire of Superhuman.

Alex Rampell, co-founder of Affirm and general partner at a16z, said, “We think businesses will soon run themselves and Lassie is the perfect example that this is not a pipe dream. They are already making this a reality, providing many businesses with tens of hours of labor each month, and allowing business owners to focus on what they love doing, not busywork.” Release

June 2— Ilant HealthValue-based obesity treatmentSeries: AAmount: $15 millionInvestors: Led by Cornucopian Capital, new participation from naturalX, Peakbridge, Semcap AI, Evidenced, Operator Partners, existing participation from Celtic, LifeX & AlphaLab

Ilant aims to deliver comprehensive, clinical care for obesity by working directly with employers and health plans. Instead of treating obesity in isolation from other health concerns, Ilant offers gains in overall wellbeing, with early results from the company showing that members achieve 15% weight loss on average. Another aspect of their mission is management of treatment costs and total cost of care, creating a platform that is easily accessible for both employers and payers.

Ilant’s AI-enabled platform seeks to create adjustable treatment plans for individuals, including both GLP-1 and non-GLP1 pathways. They also offer options for behavioral therapy and surgery, while aiming to address nutrition, physical activity, mental health and obesity. By utilizing AI, they seek to avoid “unnecessary or ineffective care,” that can stall an individual’s progress and cost more money for both employers and payers.

Ilant was founded by Elina Onitkansky, who formerly worked at both McKinsey and Molina Healthcare. In the recent press release, she states: “If we don’t change how care is delivered, we’re just paying more for the same broken system, and we risk a crisis where both chronic disease and costs are spiraling out of control. Ilant’s model focuses on delivering real value with manageable treatment costs and clinically meaningful care that actually bends the cost curve.”

June 2—Adaptive Innovations  AI in-home health providerSeries: AAmount: $50 millionInvestors: Led by Felicis and Bain Capital Ventures, with participation from Optum Ventures, Sunflower Capital, Conviction, BoxGroup, SV Angels, Dorm Room Fund and Constellation

As one of the largest home health care providers in Texas, Adaptive Innovations aims to reduce the cost and complexity of providing this care through their AI native model. Statistics from the company’s site claim that two of five patients prescribed in home care never receive it, and that the most acute 5% of patients account for over half of overall healthcare spending. The combination of these statistics means that the delivery of home health services needs to change, so Adaptive Innovations seeks to consolidate the market of at-home care and reduce administrative overheads.

With an initial seed capital of $10 million dollars, they have “delivered over 100,000 visits and partnered with 500+ referring healthcare organizations, including every major Texas hospital system,” since 2025. Building on their success, they will utilize their new funding to expand into more states and grow their team. Their recent press release serves as a call to action and recruitment for new team members interested in serving their mission of automating in home health care.

June 2—NovelliaPatient-controlled data platformSeries: AAmount: $18 millionInvestors:  Spark Capital with participation from Khosla Ventures, Acrew Capital, Bling Capital, and TMV

Novellia is tackling one of pharma’s biggest R&D challenges. Researchers have long depended on real-world data to understand how treatments perform outside clinical trials. But data is still largely stitched together from third-party sources, taking data from insurance claims and hospital records. This leaves gaps in longitudinal records that limit its value in clinical settings.

Novellia works directly with patients to compile and share their records with scientists to advance medical discoveries. The company says it puts this de-identified, anonymized data in the hands of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies and its customers include several of the top 10 pharma and early-stage diagnostics companies.

Along with the new funding, the startup also launched its patient-facing mobile app. Through Novellia’s platform, patients with serious and complex conditions can find and unify up to 20 years of medical data from disparate hospital systems, doctors' offices and labs across the U.S. The company then analyzes those records using proprietary natural language processing models that extract signals from unstructured clinical text, including physician notes, lab narratives and diagnostic reports, turning raw patient data into anonymized, harmonized datasets ready for research. Through Novellia’s platform, patients gain a free, unified view of their health history, while researchers unlock complete, consented, de-identified data for clinical trials and medical breakthroughs, according to the company. Release

May 28—H1Healthcare data platform transforming operations with AISeries: UnlabeledAmount: $40 millionInvestors: CVS Health Ventures

Health tech company H1 is focused on connecting people to the right doctor and it built an AI-powered platform that hosts healthcare provider profiles for life science, provider, health plan and digital health customers. The company claims that 85% of the top 20 pharma companies and 9 out of 10 of the top health plans are customers.

Last year, H1 picked up provider data management software company Ribbon Health to broaden its reach into the health plan, provider system and digital health sectors. Later in 2025, the healthcare tech company acquired Veda Data Solutions to build out its provider data and automation solutions for payers.

The $40 million investment from CVS’ venture capital investment arm follows H1’s collaboration with the healthcare company on several projects. H1 is working with CVS on a joint strategic AI roadmap that includes a AI model to improve CVS Health’s healthcare provider directory.

Justin Brock, Partner at CVS Health Ventures, said, “We are excited to see how H1’s data and AI capabilities can further drive efficiency and improve the consumer experience across the healthcare ecosystem.”

H1 has seen significant growth and is now profitable, Ariel Katz, co-founder and CEO of H1. There is strong demand for H1’s doctor intelligence, Katz said, and the company’s accurate doctor information is crucial for AI companies and large healthcare entities like CVS.

The company boasts that it has one of the most comprehensive global datasets of healthcare professionals and its platform combines deep healthcare data with agentic AI workflows to power critical workflows across drug development, medical and commercial engagement, care navigation, and provider data and network intelligence.

With the fresh capital, H1 plans to expand its work with health plans, Katz said. Release

May 27—SignosExpanding CGM from diabetes into weight managementSeries: unlabeledAmount: $20 millionInvestors: GV (Google Ventures), Dexcom and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alabama

Powered by a continuous glucose monitor (CGM), Signos' mobile AI-driven system offers personalized insights into how food, movement, sleep, stress, and more affect each unique body. Signos is the only FDA-cleared CGM system for weight management and requires no prescription.

Dexcom's signals strong industry interest in the expanding role of glucose biosensing beyond diabetes management. As part of a partnership with Dexcom, Signos will be available for purchase on Stelo.com, Dexcom's direct-to-consumer CGM website, making it easier for people to find and access the Signos system.

"Signos has developed a system that translates glucose biosensing data into actionable insights for people focused on weight management," Jon Coleman, Chief Commercial Officer at Dexcom, said in a statement. "Making Signos available on Stelo.com is a natural next step. It makes a powerful, FDA-cleared technology even more accessible for people who are already looking for smarter ways to manage their weight and health."

Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alabama's participation via 450 Ventures also marks validation from the payer community and recognition that metabolic health tools like Signos represent a proactive, cost-effective path to better member outcomes, Signos executives said.

The company says its grown 10-fold over the past six months, driven by increasing consumer demand for more personalized approaches to weight control. Glucose data from Dexcom’s Stelo glucose biosensor is processed through Signos' proprietary AI to provide a unique feedback loop tied to each user's unique metabolic patterns. Users learn which specific foods drive their glucose higher, which meals keep them in range, and how small adjustments accumulate into meaningful, lasting change.

For individuals taking GLP-1 medications, Signos builds the metabolic self-knowledge that supports weight management over the long term, rather than relying solely on appetite suppression, according to the company.

"Making Signos available on Stelo.com is a natural next step. It makes a powerful, FDA-cleared technology even more accessible for people who are already looking for smarter ways to manage their weight and health."

"The weight management category is being completely reimagined right now, and the approaches that will endure are the ones that combine the best of medication with the best of personalized data," said Sharam Fouladgar-Mercer, CEO and founder of Signos. Release

May 27—Triomicsoncology AI for cancer centersSeries: BAmount: $22 millionInvestors: Led by Battery Ventures, with participation from existing investors Nexus Venture Partners, Lightspeed and Y Combinator, alongside strategic backers Oncology Ventures and Precision Health Informatics, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Texas Oncology

Founded in 2021 by Sarim Khan and Hrituraj Singh, Triomics helps cancer centers operationalize complex clinical information. The company is building a platform that uses AI agents to read the full longitudinal patient record and converts unstructured information into structured, explainable outputs. It then delivers those insights directly into clinical and operational workflows. The platform supports proactive clinical trial matching, pre-visit chart review and preparation, and oncology data abstraction for registry, quality improvement and operational use cases.

Beyond provider workflows, Triomics has built a broader oncology network that helps life-sciences organizations with their critical clinical-trial operations.

Cancer centers rely on Triomics to expand trial access, reduce the burden of manual chart review, improve visit preparation and generate higher‑quality structured data for research and operations. Published results show that users of the company's product have increased trial matches by 40% and trial enrollments by more than 30%, while also reducing chart review times by 67%.

Triomics will use the fresh capital to accelerate adoption across health systems, oncology networks and life sciences organizations and grow its AI/engineering and forward-deployed teams. The company also plans to build out AI agents for clinical care and research.

Triomics says it works with leading cancer centers like Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK), MD Anderson, Yale Cancer Center and its partner Smilow Cancer Hospital, and Mount Sinai Tisch Cancer Center, as well as some of the nation's largest community oncology practices, such as Texas Oncology.

May 27—SONDEarbuds that promote better sleepSeries: unlabeledAmount: $7 millionInvestors: E14 Fund (an MIT-affiliated fund), Crosslink Capital, Ubiquity Ventures, Alumni Ventures, Meach Cove Capital, and Boston Scientific co-founder, John Abele

Boston-based startup SOND emerged from stealth with $7 million in funding and debuted its sleep earbuds called Dreambuds. The  in-ear devices can capture 12 physiological signals and uses a cloud-based AI coach to actively intervene and improve sleep in real time.

The starup was founded by a pair of MIT grads, Yadid Ayzenberg, Bose’s former Head of Global Sleep, and Amir Lazarovich, a former senior engineering manager at Google.

The device tracks signals like respiration, heart rate variability, cardiorespiratory coupling, sleep staging, body position, snoring, and seismocardiography (SCG, or the mechanical vibrations of the chest wall produced by the beating heart), as TechCrunch reports.

The sensor data streams in real time to a cloud-based AI sleep coach that then selects a sleep audio program, or generates one on demand, learning over time which ones work best for the individual user. TechCrunch story

It has partnered with large enterprise employers and pharmaceutical companies for its virtual cardiometabolic care, including support for patients with obesity, diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia. It says it has generated more than $50 million in medical and pharmacy savings across two Fortune 100 employers.

"What makes this possible is our ability to combine specialized clinical care with AI-enabled clinical workflows and personalized member experiences that allow us to scale efficiently across complex chronic conditions," said Frank Westermann, 9amHealth CEO and co-founder, in a statement. It plans to use the new funding to continue its growth as it expands into specialty-level chronic conditions that are typically high cost, collectively accounting for up to 70% of employer pharmacy spend. Release
